title: Hot Stamping Temperature Guide for Paper Boxes

seo.title: Hot Stamping Temperature Guide for Paper Boxes

content:
Temperature is one of the most important settings in hot stamping for paper boxes. It helps the foil transfer from the carrier film to the packaging surface and affects adhesion, edge clarity and metallic brightness.

## What Happens When Temperature Is Too Low

If temperature is too low, the foil may not transfer completely. Small text may break, solid areas may show missing spots and adhesion may be weak. Operators may think the foil is unsuitable, but the process may simply be under-activated.

## What Happens When Temperature Is Too High

Excessive heat can create a different set of problems. Edges may become blurry, lines may look thicker, the background may become dirty and the metallic gloss may look dull. On laminated or coated paper, too much heat can also affect the surface finish.

## How to Find the Right Window

Start with the supplier’s suggested range, then test three levels: low, middle and high. Keep pressure and contact time stable during the first test. Compare fine text, the logo and a solid area.

If transfer is incomplete, increase temperature gradually. If edges become unclear, reduce temperature and check whether pressure is too high.

## FAQ

### Should I solve every problem by increasing temperature?

No. More heat can improve transfer, but it can also cause blurry edges or dull gloss.

### Why does one paper need a different temperature from another?

Different coatings, smoothness and surface treatments change how the foil bonds.
